objectives: This course introduces students to the strategic interactions of economic agents, such as consumers, firms, and regulators, with a focus on business applications and managerial decision-making process that enable students to understand, formulate, and solve games systematically. Some basic understanding of calculus and probability is expected.
content: This course will cover the following content.1. Sequential move games2. Dominance solvable games3. Pure strategy Nash equilibrium4. Mixed strategy Nash equilibrium5. Subgame perfect Nash equilibrium6. Games of repeated interactions7. Bayesian Nash equilibrium8. Perfect Bayesian equilibrium9. Semi-separating equilibrium10. Intuitive and Divinity Criterion11. Signaling games12. Screening games13. Cheap talk games14. Evolutionary games
